newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends firm on wheat/soybean rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends firm on wheat/soybean rally.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firm on a late rally in wheat and soybean futures, traders said.
But volume was thin before the release Wednesday of USDA's February supply/demand report, traders said.
"The main thing will be the numbers tomorrow. Today we're just evening up," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
At 0730 CST Wednesday, USDA will release updated figures for 1996-97 U.S. carryout and also could adjust its outlook for corn production in several other countries.
Slow farmer selling underpinned prices but talk about near ideal crop weather in South America limited gains.
The U.S. Agriculture Attache this week raised to 14.5 million tonnes from the previous 13.5 million its estimate for this year's Argentine maize production.
The Argentine government's Agricultural Secretariat has pegged Argentine maize output at 14.6 million tonnes.
Corn closed unchanged to one cent per bushel higher, with March up 1/2 at $2.72-1/2.
Chartists early Tuesday cited first resistance in March corn at $2.72-1/2 and second resistance at $2.74. The session high for March was $2.72-3/4.
First support for March was $2.71 and second support was $2.69-1/2. The session low for March was $2.71.

The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for March remains near neutral territory and closed at 56 percent. The trade generally considers an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold market and 70 or more as an overbought market.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 35,000 contracts, slightly above the 34,420 traded Monday.
Corn options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, above the 8,111 traded Monday.
